facts.text: On this date in 1949, Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Square — a nation that now holds more foreign currency reserves than the next five countries combined.
On this date in 1960, Nigeria gained independence. It is now Africa's most populous country, with more English speakers than the United Kingdom.
More people live within a 4,000km radius centered on Bangladesh than outside it — over half of humanity packed into roughly a third of Earth's land.
Vatican City generates more revenue per square meter than any nation on Earth, largely through museum admissions, postage stamps, and a surprisingly active publishing house.
Manila is the most densely populated city on the planet — over 111,000 people per square kilometer, nearly double the density of second-place Dhaka.

On this day in 1903, the New York Stock Exchange installed its first ticker-tape telephone system — traders could now get prices without shouting across a room, ending Wall Street's era of pure chaos.
On October 1, 1979, the Tokyo Stock Exchange reopened to foreign membership for the first time since WWII, cracking open what would become the world's second-largest equity market.
The S&P 500 has never ended a 20-year rolling period in the red — not once, across every start date since the index existed.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A share has never been split. At over $700,000 per share, it is the highest-priced stock on any major exchange by a factor of hundreds.
The Dutch East India Company, the first firm to issue tradable shares, paid dividends continuously for nearly 200 years — often in spices rather than cash.
On this date in 1958, NASA officially opened for business — a civilian agency born from military panic after Sputnik, tasked with making space feel peaceful while the Cold War burned beneath it.

On October 1st, 1880, John Philip Sousa took over the U.S. Marine Band. Within a decade he had reinvented what a brass ensemble could do — but that belongs to music. In 1880, the germ theory of disease was still a fight, not a fact.
Your red blood cells have no nucleus. They evict their own DNA to make room for more hemoglobin, then live for 120 days as hollow, oxygen-ferrying husks before being quietly dismantled in the spleen.

A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth — not metaphorically, but by straightforward gravitational calculation.

Light leaving the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth, but the energy in that light took roughly 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface, crawling through dense plasma one collision at a time.
On this day in 1908, the Ford Model T went on sale. It outlasted the Ottoman Empire, which wouldn't collapse for another 14 years.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the civilization Cortés destroyed.
On this day in 1949, Mao declared the People's Republic of China. The Soviet Union recognized it the next day; the US waited 30 years.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before the lightbulb. Japan was still using it in the 2020s.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home you cannot return to — or that never existed. Untranslatable in a single English word, it carries grief, nostalgia, and belonging simultaneously.

On this day in 1800, the Combination Acts passed in Britain, outlawing worker unions. The word 'strike' for labor stoppage predates them, likely from sailors who 'struck' — lowered — their sails to stop a ship.
On Oct 1, 1949, Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China. The Mandarin name, Zhōngguó (中国), means 'Middle Kingdom' — not the center of Asia, but the civilized world between heaven and barbarism.

Petrichor (n.): the smell of rain on dry earth. Named in 1964 by Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and R.G. Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid said to flow through the veins of the gods.
On this day in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto registered bitcoin.org — 18 days before publishing the whitepaper. The domain predates the protocol's public existence.
On this day in 2020, Uniswap airdropped 400 UNI to every historical user. At peak prices, each claim was worth over $16,000 — retroactive value for wallets that had simply existed.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, wasn't named by Satoshi. The term was proposed by a forum user in 2010 and adopted by community consensus — Nakamoto was already gone.
Ethereum's gas limit is not hardcoded. Miners — now validators — vote it up or down each block, making Ethereum's throughput a rolling social consensus rather than a protocol constant.
The FBI became one of Bitcoin's largest holders after seizing Silk Road funds in 2013. At one point it controlled roughly 1.5% of all circulating BTC — an accidental sovereign fund.

On this date in 1958, Frank Rosenblatt demonstrated the Perceptron at Cornell — the first machine to learn from experience by adjusting weights. The architecture it introduced still underlies every modern neural network.
On this date in 2015, Google announced it had begun using RankBrain, a neural network, to process a significant fraction of all search queries — without telling the web for months.

GPT-4's training run consumed an estimated 50 petaflop/s-days of compute. AlexNet, which shocked the vision community in 2012, required roughly 0.0003 petaflop/s-days — a 150,000-fold gap in 12 years.

Transformers were not invented to do language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation specifically; the architecture's generality was a discovery made afterward, not a design goal.

Chinchilla scaling laws showed that most large models released before 2022 were simultaneously undertrained and overparameterized — meaning researchers had been spending compute in roughly the wrong ratio for years.
